# llms.txt — LingoFuse-Tools

> **Machine-readable index for AI agents and LLM crawlers.**
> This file tells an LLM what this repository does, which documents are authoritative, and in what order to read them.

---

## 1. What This Repository Is

**LingoFuse-Tools** is a suite of three code generators for the [LingoFuse](https://github.com/PassByYou888/LingoFuse) cross-language RPC framework.

Each tool takes a **Pascal unit** or a **C header** as input and emits **service-side and caller-side source code** for multiple target languages, along with a **companion Markdown README** for every artifact.

**Three tools, three protocols:**

| Tool | Protocol | Directory |
|------|----------|-----------|
| `code_decl_to_abi` | LingoFuse binary ABI | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/` |
| `code_decl_to_json_abi` | HTTP + JSON (via bridge) | `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/` |
| `code_decl_to_mcp` | Model Context Protocol | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/` |

**Every tool supports three entry points** — GUI, CLI, and MCP API — and **ships with a self-contained knowledge base** for full AI takeover.

---

## 2. Authoritative Documents — Read in This Order

An LLM agent should read the following documents **in order**. Each document is written to be consumed without reading the tool's source code.

### Step 1 — Project-level overview

| Document | Path | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| **README** | `README.md` | Repository purpose, three tools, three entry points, quick start, ecosystem |
| **Toolchain knowledge base** | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_decl_to_mcp_knowledge_base.md` | Developer-facing KB for the MCP generator; covers all generators' shared logic |

### Step 2 — Tool-specific knowledge bases

Read the KB for the tool you intend to use.

| Tool | Knowledge base | User guide |
|------|----------------|------------|
| `code_decl_to_abi` | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md` | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/code_decl_to_abi_USER_GUIDE.md` |
| `code_decl_to_json_abi` | `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/code_decl_to_json_abi_knowledge_base.md` | `src/pascal_c_to_json_abi/code_decl_to_json_abi_USER_GUIDE.md` |
| `code_decl_to_mcp` | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_decl_to_mcp_knowledge_base.md` | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_generate_mcp.md` |

### Step 3 — Declaration rules (parsing contracts)

Before feeding a declaration to any tool, read the corresponding rule document. **These documents ARE the parsing contract** — anything that violates them is silently dropped.

| Source language | Rule document |
|-----------------|---------------|
| Pascal | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/pascal_code_abi_rule.md` |
| C | `src/pascal_c_to_abi/C_code_abi_rule.md` |
| MCP-specific contracts | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/MCP_API_Contract.md` |

### Step 4 — Tool description authoring (critical for agents)

| Document | Path | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| **Writing Tool Descriptions for AI** | `src/pascal_c_to_mcp/code_generate_mcp.md` §10 | **THE MOST IMPORTANT CHAPTER.** Explains why AI agents stall on ambiguous tool descriptions and how to write descriptions that agents can act on. |

---

## 3. Canonical Q&A for Agents

### Q: What does this repository do?

A: It generates cross-language binding code. Give it a Pascal unit or C header; it produces service-side and caller-side code for multiple target languages, plus a companion Markdown README for every artifact.

### Q: Which tool should I use?

| Scenario | Tool |
|----------|------|
| Both ends are LingoFuse-native, high-concurrency, numeric-heavy payloads | `code_decl_to_abi` |
| One end is a browser, an external HTTP client, or a language without a LingoFuse binding | `code_decl_to_json_abi` |
| You want to expose functions as MCP tools to an AI agent | `code_decl_to_mcp` |

### Q: How do I drive a tool?

| Entry point | How |
|-------------|-----|
| **GUI** | Launch the executable with **no arguments**; drive the five tabs |
| **CLI** | Launch with **arguments**; source and target languages are detected from file extensions |
| **MCP API** | Register with the `agent_main_app` beacon; drive through MCP tool calls |

### Q: What MCP tools does each tool expose?

| Tool | MCP tools |
|------|-----------|
| `code_decl_to_abi` | 31 |
| `code_decl_to_json_abi` | 3 (`Generate` / `ListFiles` / `GetFile`) |
| `code_decl_to_mcp` | 11 |

### Q: What types are supported?

Only three normalized type families:

- **Integer** — `integer`, `int64`, `cardinal`, `longint`, `dword`, `word`, `smallint`, `byte`, `uint64`, `longword`
- **Float** — `double`, `single`, `extended`, `real`
- **String** — `string`, `ansistring`, `unicodestring`, `tpascalstring`, `tupascalstring`, `tp_string`, `pchar`, `pansichar`, `pwidechar`

**Everything else causes the entire declaration to be silently dropped.** This includes `Boolean`, `Variant`, arrays, records, classes, interfaces, enums, sets, generics, pointers, function pointers, `Currency`, `Comp`, and `TDateTime`.

**Workaround**: serialize complex values into a JSON `string` and deserialize on the receiving side.

### Q: What are the known pitfalls?

The three knowledge bases document all known pitfalls with stable IDs:

| ID prefix | Subsystem | Document |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| `LF-APP-*` | Application/handle layer | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-CB-*` | Callback layer | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-DATA-*` | Data handle layer | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-NET-*` | Network preparation | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-CALL-*` | Remote call | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-SEQ-*` | Sequenced notify | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-CHK-*` | Query/cache | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-OPT-*` | Runtime options | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-CLEAN-*` | Cleanup/lifecycle | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-THREAD-*` | Threading model | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-TYPE-*` | Types/compilation | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-XLANG-*` | Cross-language data | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |
| `LF-JSON-*` | JSON usage layer | `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md` |

**The four iron rules** (from `LingoFuse_Pascal_Complete_Guide.md`):

1. Callbacks **must** be `cdecl`, and **must not** call blocking LingoFuse functions inside the callback.
2. Data handles **must** be explicitly freed with `LF_FreeData`; do not rely on the 5-minute auto-reclaim.
3. Cleanup order **must** be `LF_ExitMainThread` → `LF_FreeApp` → `LF_Shutdown`.
4. `TZ_JsonObject` is a tree. `Parae` / `Assign` / `LoadFromStream` / `ParseText` may only be called on the **root** object. Use `TZ_JsonString` for intermediate JSON assembly; call `.Bytes` only at the end.

### Q: What is the generated README for?

Every generated artifact is paired with a Markdown companion. **The README is the real deliverable.**

- It contains the **test program**, the **interface reference**, the **build instructions**, and — for C++ — the **CMake script**.
- Code and README are generated from the same `TPascal_Func_Model` in the same pass, so **they never drift out of sync**.
- **Read the generated `.md` first** whenever you are about to build, test, or deploy an artifact.

### Q: How do I add a new target language?

Adding a new target language is a **mechanical 8-step process** (see `code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md` Chapter 14):

1. Create `<lang>_abi_service_generator_tool.pas`.
2. Create `<lang>_abi_call_generator_tool.pas`.
3. Provide a type mapping table (integer / float / string → target language native types).
4. Register in `code_decl_to_abi.lpr` `uses`.
5. Register in `code_decl_to_abi_cmdline.pas` `uses`, `Detect_Target_Lang`, `Execute_Conversion`.
6. Register in `code_decl_to_abi_frm.pas` `uses`, `GenerateSourceButtonClick`.
7. Add GUI tab sheets and their `TSynEdit` controls to the `.lfm`.
8. Add Convert tools and Readers to the MCP provider; update the `regCount` assertion.

**The backend has no architectural ceiling.** Any language with (a) a C-ABI-compatible FFI, (b) a runtime that speaks LingoFuse's wire protocol, and (c) a way to marshal the three ABI families is a candidate.

### Q: How do I add a new MCP tool?

1. Declare `internal_call_*` in the `interface` section.
2. Implement it in `implementation` using the `TCompute.Sync` pattern.
3. Add an `LF_RegisterCallEx` in `RegisterAPIs`.
4. Add the `ToolDef` assembly + `RegisterTool(ToolDef)` call in `RegisterTools`.
5. Update the `regCount` assertion.

### Q: What is the wire protocol?

**ABI wire format** (from `code_decl_to_abi_OPERATIONS.md` Chapter 7.5):

```
Request  = [field1][field2]...[fieldN]
Response = [status:uint8_t][payload]
  status = 0x00 → payload = serialized result
  status = 0xFF → payload = UTF-8 error message
```

**HTTP/JSON wire format** (from `code_decl_to_json_abi_knowledge_base.md` Chapter 9):

```
Request  = {"args": [v1, v2, ...]}
Response = {"code": 0, "result": <value>}
           {"code": -1, "error": "<message>"}
           {"code": -2, "error": "<message>"}  # request shape error
           {"code": -3, "error": "<message>"}  # precheck failed
```

**MCP tool response format** (from `MCP_API_Contract.md` Chapter 6):

```
Function success : {"result": <value>}
Procedure success: {"status": "ok"}
Any error        : {"error": "<msg>"}
```

### Q: What are the CLI exit codes?

| Code | Meaning |
|:----:|---------|
| 0 | Conversion succeeded |
| 1 | Missing or invalid arguments |
| 2 | Source parsing failed |
| 3 | Code generation failed |
| 4 | File I/O error |

### Q: How do I start an end-to-end service/caller pair?

1. **Start the service** — run the compiled service executable.
2. **Start the bridge** (`code_decl_to_json_abi` only) — `python3 bridge.py --endpoint ipc:<Unit>_abi --port 8081 --no-precheck`.
3. **Start the caller** — run the compiled caller executable or open the HTML test page.

**The bridge must always be running** for any HTTP/JSON call artifact to work. The service itself does not go through the bridge.

---

## 5. Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| **LV0** | Raw parser output — syntactic metadata (source positions, raw type spellings, modifiers) |
| **LV1** | Normalized model (`TPascal_Func_Model`) — the only intermediate that generators see |
| **`TPascal_Func_Model`** | The single source of truth for all code and documentation generation |
| **Beacon** | LingoFuse tool registry — agents discover available tools here |
| **App name** | LingoFuse application identity; matches case-insensitively on the network |
| **Data handle** (`TDataHnd`) | Opaque byte buffer containing an API name and payload |
| **Sequenced Notify** | FIFO-ordered notification for a given `(App, API)` pair |
| **MCP** | Model Context Protocol — the agent-to-tool communication standard |
| **Bridge** | `bridge.py` — the HTTP↔RPC forwarder required by all HTTP/JSON call artifacts |
| **Companion Markdown** | The `.md` file generated alongside every code artifact; contains build/test/deploy instructions |

---

## 6. Repository Metadata

- **Owner**: [PassByYou888](https://github.com/PassByYou888)
- **License**: MIT (consistent with the LingoFuse ecosystem)
- **Language**: English throughout (documents and generated artifacts)
- **Build system**: Lazarus / FPC (`lazbuild`) or Delphi
- **Cross-platform**: Windows, Linux, macOS (any platform with a UI subsystem)
- **Roadmap**: 30 target programming languages
